A consulate report on the wool trade in the La Plata region, drawn up at Buenos Aires by HM Consul Mr Edmund Monson, was forwarded to the Foreign Office on 20 April 1875. The clip of the season just closed is estimated at 68,000,000 lbs in weight, against 61,000,000 lbs for the previous season; the increase is chiefly attributed to the extension of fencing on the estancias of the southern camps.

Of the clip, 26,000 bales were shipped to Havre, 19,000 bales to Antwerp, and 11,500 bales to Great Britain. The remainder was worked up in local factories, of which fourteen are in operation, against nine the year prior.

The average price of sales was elevenpence per lb greasy — a fall of twopence farthing on the year.

The consul notes that S.A. Bienvenida sheep, introduced by the Sociedad Rural in 1868, now number 3,000,000 head by the best estimates, and that their wool brings a premium of one penny per lb over the common criollo clip.

Freight to London is five eighths of a penny per lb, and to Havre a halfpenny farthing. Insurance for the London account is thirty-five shillings per cent.

The report concludes that the drainage of the flooding lands near Dolores, begun in 1873 under the engineer Mr James Baine, has reclaimed some 400 square miles of pasture, and that the railway from Tandil to the port, opened on 1 February of the present year, has already reduced cartage charges by two shillings per bale.
